target: n2, p1, court.section, imports.formal-notice (p2, b5), e5
claim: For a sale on plans (البيع على التصاميم) under the real-estate promotion law, a subscriber's failure to pay two successive instalments rescinds the contract by law, but only after two notices of fifteen days each, served by a bailiff, that went unanswered. The record has no boundary for this contract: a promoter suing to rescind would get the general article 119 route, with the imported single notice rule (which accepts post or an agreed default), and nothing would check the two bailiff notices or the 15-day periods.

source.what: Law 11-04 of 17 February 2011 setting the rules of real-estate promotion, art. 53 ¶1-2; Official Journal no. 14 of 6 March 2011, page 10 (law heading on page 4). No later amendment of art. 53 found (web search only: a 2024 ministerial announcement of a draft amendment, no published amending law found).

quoteArabic: يتعين على المكتتب في عقد البيع على التصاميم دفع التسديدات التي تقع على عاتقه في الآجال المنصوص عليها، وفي حالة عدم التسديد، يحتفظ المرقي العقاري بحق توقيع عقوبة على المبلغ المستحق. يترتب على عدم تسديد دفعتين متتاليتين فسخ العقد بحكم القانون بعد إعذارين، مدة كل واحد منهما خمسة عشر (15) يوما، يبلغان عن طريق محضر قضائي، ولم يتم الرد عليهما.
consequence: Add a boundary (or a prior step) for a sale on plans: when a promoter seeks rescission for unpaid instalments, check two successive unpaid instalments and two bailiff-served notices of 15 days each that went unanswered, and treat the rescission as one by law (like n2), not one the judge decides under article 119. Note also CPCA 512 ¶4 (store text: «ينظر القسم العقاري على الخصوص ... 3- في نشاط الترقية العقارية»): disputes over real-estate promotion go to the real-estate section, which the section rule reaches only if the lawyer answers dispute_concerns_real_property = yes.

claim: For an online (e-commerce) sale to a consumer, the e-commerce law gives the buyer its own remedy for late delivery and for goods that do not match the order or are defective: he sends the goods back within four working days from actual delivery, and the supplier must refund within fifteen days. It also makes the supplier liable by force of law, cleared only by the consumer's act or force majeure. The record treats non-delivery or late delivery only under Civil Code 119 and defective delivery only under the warranty of 379/383 (one year, boundary n3). It has no question about an online sale, and no warning about the four-working-day window that runs from actual delivery.

source.what: Law 18-05 on e-commerce (dated 10 May 2018 from memory; issue dated 16 May 2018), arts. 22 and 23 (page 8) and art. 18 (page 7), Official Journal no. 28 of 2018.

quoteArabic: المادة 22: في حالة عدم احترام المورد الإلكتروني لآجال التسليم، يمكن المستهلك الإلكتروني إعادة إرسال المنتوج على حالته في أجل أقصاه أربعة (4) أيام عمل ابتداء من تاريخ التسليم الفعلي للمنتوج، دون المساس بحقه في المطالبة بالتعويض عن الضرر. وفي هذه الحالة، يجب على المورد الإلكتروني أن يرجع إلى المستهلك الإلكتروني المبلغ المدفوع والنفقات المتعلقة بإعادة إرسال المنتوج، خلال أجل خمسة عشر (15) يوما ابتداء من تاريخ استلامه المنتوج. المادة 23: يجب على المورد الإلكتروني استعادة سلعته في حالة تسليم غرض غير مطابق للطلبية أو في حالة ما إذا كان المنتوج معيبا. يجب على المستهلك الإلكتروني إعادة إرسال السلعة في غلافها الأصلي، خلال مدة أقصاها أربعة (4) أيام عمل ابتداء من تاريخ التسليم الفعلي للمنتوج ... المادة 18 (¶2): غير أنه، يمكن المورد الإلكتروني أن يتحلل من كامل مسؤوليته أو جزء منها إذا أثبت أن عدم التنفيذ أو سوءه يعود إلى المستهلك الإلكتروني أو إلى قوة قاهرة.
consequence: Add a question (was this an online sale by an e-supplier to a consumer?) and a boundary. For late delivery or non-conforming or defective goods, point to Law 18-05 arts. 22 and 23: return within 4 working days of actual delivery, refund within 15 days of the supplier receiving the goods, damages kept. Tell the lawyer to check whether the return was made within the window before drafting a judicial rescission. The n3 message (one-year warranty) is not the whole answer for such a sale.

claim: The record lists the contract, invoices, receipts, correspondence and bailiff or expert reports as documents to attach, but does not say that every document produced must be in Arabic or come with an official translation into Arabic, on pain of inadmissibility. In this claim, contracts, invoices and commercial correspondence are often in French.

source.what: Law 08-09 of 25 February 2008 (Code of Civil and Administrative Procedure), art. 8 ¶2; Official Journal no. 21 of 23 April 2008, page 4. Not touched by Law 22-13 according to the amendment ledger.

quoteArabic: يجب أن تقدم الوثائق والمستندات باللغة العربية أو مصحوبة بترجمة رسمية إلى هذه اللغة، تحت طائلة عدم القبول.
consequence: The document list (doc1 to doc4, and the imported formal-notice documents) should state that documents not in Arabic need an official translation, on pain of inadmissibility (CPCA 8 ¶2), and ask or warn when the contract or invoices are in another language.

claim: Common case: the seller of real property (or of a business) sells by notarial deed and later sues to rescind for unpaid price. Since 324 bis 1, the price must be paid before the notary, and the notarial deed that records the payment is proof until shown to be forged. The record's e5 says only that the debtor proves payment. Nothing warns that an unpaid-price claim contradicting a notarial deed fails unless the deed is challenged for forgery, or that witnesses cannot be used against it. The record would draft the claim silently.

source.what: Civil Code art. 324 bis 1 ¶1 and art. 324 bis 5 ¶1 (inserted by Law 88-14, Official Journal no. 18 of 4 May 1988, pp. 749-751 according to the ledger), read in the article store text view (civil-code.txt); art. 334 ¶1-2 (Law 05-10 wording). The Official Journal page itself was not fetched for this attack.

quoteArabic: ويجب دفع الثمن لدى الضابط العمومي الذي حرر العقد. ... يعتبر ما ورد في العقد الرسمي حجة حتى يثبت تزويره. ... لا يجوز الإثبات بالشهود ولو لم تزد القيمة على 100.000 دينار جزائري: – فيما يخالف أو يجاوز ما اشتمل عليه مضمون عقد رسمي،
consequence: When the plaintiff is the seller under an official deed and the ground is the unpaid price, ask whether the deed records payment before the notary. If it does, warn that the claim needs a forgery challenge (طعن بالتزوير) against that statement, and that witnesses are not admitted against the deed.

claim: Boundary n8 (nullity for want of official form) fires only when dispute_concerns_real_property = yes. Article 324 bis 1 also requires official form, on pain of nullity, for transfers of a business (محل تجاري أو صناعي, or any element of it), for transfers of company shares or parts, and for commercial and agricultural leases and management leases. The common case of rescinding an informal (private-deed) sale of a business or of company shares gets no form warning.

source.what: Civil Code art. 324 bis 1 ¶1 (Law 88-14), as quoted in the record's own b25 and in the store text view; Official Journal page not fetched.

quoteArabic: يجب، تحت طائلة البطلان، تحرير العقود التي تتضمن نقل ملكية عقار أو حقوق عقارية أو محلات تجارية أو صناعية أو كل عنصر من عناصرها، أو التنازل عن أسهم من شركة أو حصص فيها، أو عقود إيجار زراعية أو تجارية أو عقود تسيير محلات تجارية أو مؤسسات صناعية في شكل رسمي
consequence: n8 (and its slot) should also fire for a sale of a business or of an element of it, and for a transfer of company shares or parts, not only for real property.

claim: Lead only. The Commercial Code's chapter on the sale of a business is recalled to set extra conditions on the seller's action to rescind for unpaid price. As recalled, the action must be expressly mentioned and reserved in the registration of the seller's privilege, and the seller must notify the creditors registered on the business before the rescission is pronounced. The record does not cover this. The store holds the Commercial Code only from article 30 and articles 169 to 202, and the amendment ledger does not cover the Commercial Code at all.

source.what: Memory of the Algerian Commercial Code (ordinance 75-59), chapter on the sale of the business, around articles 96 to 117 (the rules modelled on the French law of 17 March 1909); article numbers and wording not verified on joradp.dz.

consequence: Fetch the Commercial Code articles on the sale of a business (Official Journal no. 101 of 1975 and later amendments) and check whether the seller's rescission action must be reserved in the registration and notified to registered creditors. If so, add a boundary or prior step for that case.

claim: Checklist line k15 says that, against a contractor who delays or works defectively, the court may set a period and then rescind or have the work completed by another, and it is marked 'applies' with no correcting note. Article 553 ¶1, as the record itself quotes it in b12, has the client (رب العمل) fix the reasonable period in his warning. The court does not set it. Completion by another contractor goes through article 170, which needs the judge's authorisation.

source.what: Civil Code art. 553 ¶1 (Law 05-10 wording) and art. 170 ¶1, article store text view civil-code.txt.

quoteArabic: جاز لرب العمل أن ينذره بأن يصحح من طريقة التنفيذ خلال أجل معقول يعينه له ... في الالتزام بعمل، اذا لم يقم المدين بتنفيذ التزامه جاز للدائن أن يطلب ترخيصا من القاضى في تنفيذ الالتزام على نفقة المدين اذا كان هذا التنفيذ ممكنا.
consequence: k15 should note that the client, not the court, fixes the period (b12, p2), and that completion at the contractor's cost needs the judge's authorisation under article 170, which the store now holds (o6 and k68 say article 170 is missing from the store; it is at civil-code 170 ¶1).
